title: All About You
tagline: Job, studies, hobbies, trips, and 'when are you settling down?'
canDo: You can talk about your life: work, hobbies, where you've been

grammar.title: Habits: -ta hoon
grammar.body: Stem + ta/ti/te + hoon/hai/hain describes habits and general facts: main London mein rehta hoon (I live in London), aap kya karte hain? (what do you do?).

grammar.title: Simple past (verbs of motion)
grammar.body: Stem + a/i/e, matching the subject: main gaya / gayi, hum gaye, woh aaya / aayi. Add tha/thi/the to push it further into the past: main Pakistan gaya tha. Transitive verbs (eat, say, do) use 'ne' instead: that's Unit 10.

phrases.note: Say it calmly. Your parents already know. They're just hoping.
Code for 'when are you getting married', with a side of 'and buying a house'.
Asked by aunties within minutes of meeting you. Legally.
The perfect non-answer to the salary question.

phrases.roman: Arre! Kaise ho? Main abhi hospital se aaya
phrases.urdu: ارے! کیسے ہو؟ میں ابھی ہسپتال سے آیا
phrases.en: Hey! How are you? I just got back from the hospital
phrases.speaker: bilal

phrases.en: I'm fine, Bilal. What's new with you?

phrases.roman: Bas, aaj teen surgery ki. Tum kya karte ho aaj kal?
phrases.urdu: بس، آج تین سرجری کیں۔ تم کیا کرتے ہو آج کل؟
phrases.en: Oh, just did three surgeries today. What are you up to these days?
phrases.speaker: bilal

phrases.roman: Main abhi parhai kar raha hoon
phrases.urdu: میں ابھی پڑھائی کر رہا ہوں

phrases.roman: Achha, engineer. Bohat achha. Mere ek patient bhi engineer hain
phrases.urdu: اچھا، انجینئر۔ بہت اچھا۔ میرے ایک مریض بھی انجینئر ہیں
phrases.en: Oh, engineer. Very nice. One of my patients is an engineer too
phrases.speaker: bilal

phrases.roman: Abhi tak parhai? Main to pachees saal mein doctor ban gaya tha
phrases.urdu: ابھی تک پڑھائی؟ میں تو پچیس سال میں ڈاکٹر بن گیا تھا
phrases.en: Still studying? I was a doctor by twenty-five
phrases.speaker: bilal

phrases.roman: Aur shauq? Main weekend pe golf khelta hoon
phrases.urdu: اور شوق؟ میں ویک اینڈ پہ گالف کھیلتا ہوں
phrases.en: And hobbies? I play golf on weekends
phrases.speaker: bilal

phrases.roman: Mujhe cricket pasand hai. Tum golf hi khelo
phrases.urdu: مجھے کرکٹ پسند ہے۔ تم گالف ہی کھیلو
phrases.en: I like cricket. You stick to golf

phrases.roman: Khana? Waah. Nani ko bataunga, khush hongi
phrases.urdu: کھانا؟ واہ۔ نانی کو بتاؤں گا، خوش ہوں گی
phrases.en: Cooking? Nice. I'll tell Nani, she'll be pleased
phrases.speaker: bilal

phrases.roman: Haha! Achha, tum Pakistan kab gaye the?
phrases.urdu: ہاہا! اچھا، تم پاکستان کب گئے تھے؟
phrases.en: Haha! Okay, when did you last go to Pakistan?
phrases.speaker: bilal

phrases.roman: Main pichhle saal Pakistan gaya tha
phrases.urdu: میں پچھلے سال پاکستان گیا تھا
phrases.en: I went to Pakistan last year
accept: main pichhle saal pakistan gaya tha
main pichhle saal pakistan gayi thi

phrases.roman: Zabardast. Chalo, mera pager baj raha hai. Phir milte hain!
phrases.urdu: زبردست۔ چلو، میرا پیجر بج رہا ہے۔ پھر ملتے ہیں!
phrases.en: Brilliant. Right, my pager's going off. See you!
phrases.speaker: bilal

teach.title: Liking activities
teach.info: 'I like cooking' = mujhe khana banana pasand hai. Use the full verb (banana, parhna, khelna) before pasand hai.

teach.tip: Every Pakistani family's shared religion, after the actual one.

exercises.prompt: Tell Nani you like reading books. (She'll approve.)

lessons.title: Main gaya tha
lessons.blurb: The simple past: went, came, slept, woke up late.
lessons.canDo: You can say where you went and what happened

teach.title: Simple past (motion verbs)
teach.info: For verbs like go, come, sleep, wake: stem + a/i/e matches the subject's gender. main gaya (I went, man), main gayi (woman), hum gaye (we went). Add 'tha' for further back: main Pakistan gaya tha.

teach.tip: Also what happens to every uncle after biryani.

exercises.prompt: Tell your friend your family went to Lahore.
You're a guy. Type: “I went to Pakistan”

lessons.title: Settle kab?
lessons.blurb: Salary, settling down, and the art of the non-answer.
lessons.canDo: You can deflect nosy questions about money and marriage politely

exercises.situation: Mrs. Butt asks your salary at a dawat.

options.feedback: Elegant. She'll never know, and she knows she'll never know.
Fair, but she'll tell everyone you're 'very private'. Which means 'unemployed'.
She asked for a number. You gave a job title. She's now guessing. Loudly.

exercises.prompt: Type the perfect non-answer: “I get by”

boss.title: Doctor Bilal
boss.blurb: Cousin Bilal, MD, wants to 'catch up'. It's a competition. It's always been a competition.
boss.scene: Eid lunch at Nani's. You're filling your plate when a hand claps your shoulder. It's Bilal, still in scrubs (on purpose), stethoscope round his neck (also on purpose).
boss.canDo: You can talk about your work, hobbies and travels with family, even Bilal

b.prompt: Answer, then turn it back on him.

options.reaction: 'Tum sunao' (you tell me): mistake. He will.
Golf burn. The uncles nearby nod in approval.

i.prompt: Talk about your last trip to Pakistan.

k.prompt: He's leaving. (Nobody has used a pager since 2003.)

end.title: Survived Doctor Bilal
end.text: Job, hobbies, past trips: all in Urdu, against the family's undefeated champion. Nani watched the whole thing. She gave you the extra kebab.
